summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated in the past by anastomotic ulcers presented with worsening abdominal pain and frequent dry heaves after prior removal of her gastrostomy tube, with concern for inadequate nutrition. She was stabilized with IV fluids including a vitamin-containing infusion and treated with IV pantoprazole twice daily while her diet was cautiously advanced; she tolerated a stage 4 bariatric diet and maintained stable vital signs and urine output. On hospital day 3 she underwent upper endoscopy, which showed expected post-bypass anatomy with unremarkable limbs and jejuno-jejunal anastomosis and only a small gastric erosion. By discharge she was tolerating a stage 5 bariatric diet, ambulating independently, and had controlled pain; she was discharged home on oral pantoprazole twice daily and sucralfate with as-needed antiemetic and short-term pain medication, along with return precautions and surgical follow-up.
